newsitem.title: UK: Sears says continues to back Strong as CEO.
newsitem.headline: Sears says continues to back Strong as CEO.

text.p: Troubled British retail group Sears Plc said on Monday it continued to back Liam Strong as chief executive and poured scorn on a report saying Strong could be axed.

Strong has come under increasing fire because of Sears' poor retail performance, a recent profits warning and stumbling progress on the sale of its Freemans home shopping business. The stock has dropped by around a fifth since January.

The Financial Mail on Sunday newspaper said at the weekend that Sears directors were preparing for a meeting on Monday that it said could lead to Strong's ousting from the post he has held for five years. Sears said the report was wrong.
"The situation is unchanged. The board continues to back Strong. The story is inaccurate," a spokesman for Sears said.
The spokesman said Sears held a routine board meeting every Monday to discuss operations. He said the meeting would not address Strong's position.
Strong has been plagued by reports forecasting his imminent demise for most of this year.

In January, Sears denied it was looking for a successor for the embattled chief executive despite reports his job had been offered to and turned down by David Jones, chief executive of retail chain Next Plc.

Other reports said institutional investors were unhappy with Sears' performance and were looking for change at the boardroom level and a break-up of the group including the profitable Selfridges department store.
Sears shares were unchanged at 75-1/2p in London on Monday morning.
